models.name: deepseek-v4-flash
models.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 8 H100 GPUs. Configs use EAGLE speculative decoding.

variants.description: TP4 on four GPUs. 149 GiB of weights do not need eight cards: halving them still leaves 61% of the KV pool, because the weights are a fixed cost that does not shrink with the card count. Measured 38.57 GiB of weights per card and max_total_num_tokens 4,002,048, against 6,524,672 at TP8. Those two numbers imply ~34 and ~68 KiB per token respectively, so neither can be used to extrapolate another TP width -- the reason for the gap is not known.
TP8 on one eight-GPU node, default MoE runner. Measured max_total_num_tokens 6,524,672.
Baseline: TP8 on eight H100 GPUs, single node.
Tuned by LLM AutoTune: TP8 on eight H100 GPUs, single node, EAGLE speculative decoding. +51% on the tuning benchmark vs the baseline variant.

TP4 on four GPUs, the vLLM counterpart of sglang-tp4-6000d. Measured 39.42 GiB per card for weights plus non-torch memory, 33.07 GiB left for KV, GPU KV cache size 3,447,225 tokens -- 3.29x the 1,048,576-token maximum request length. The engine's own suggestion is to raise the KV allocation to 40.08 GiB with --kv-cache-memory, which is left off here because it has not been load-tested.
TP8 on one eight-GPU RTX 6000D node. Single-node, so no RDMA and no host networking.

models.name: deepseek-v4-flash-0731-nvfp4
models.description: NVIDIA's NVFP4 build of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (routed experts in NVFP4, attention and shared experts in FP8) on RTX 6000D: SGLang or vLLM with TP4 or TP8 on one node, or vLLM prefill/decode-disaggregated (xPyD, TP8 per instance). The FP4 kernels require Blackwell GPUs.

variants.description: NVIDIA's NVFP4 build with TP4 on four RTX 6000D GPUs. Measured: ready in ~6.5 min, 40.94 GB of weights per card, KV ~3.6M tokens. Two fit one node. --moe-runner-backend=marlin is required: the default trtllm backend has no sm120 kernels, and flashinfer_cutlass serves but silently miscomputes (identical temperature-0 requests answer 23*47 as 161, 1721, 1551); marlin was correct and stable. /root/.cache is a hostPath so compiled kernels survive a restart.

NVIDIA's NVFP4 build with TP8 on one RTX 6000D node. Measured: ready in ~7 min on a cold cache, KV 6,274,304 tokens, deployed with this chart. --moe-runner-backend=marlin is required: the default trtllm backend has no sm120 kernels, and flashinfer_cutlass serves but silently miscomputes (identical temperature-0 requests answer 23*47 as 161, 1721, 1551); marlin was correct and stable. /root/.cache is a hostPath so compiled kernels survive a restart.

NVIDIA's NVFP4 build (NVFP4 routed experts, FP8 elsewhere) with TP4 on four RTX 6000D GPUs, single node. FlashInfer autotune is off: with it on, vLLM v0.30.0 hangs on these cards at the whole-model autotune pass. /root/.cache is a hostPath so compiled kernels survive a restart.

NVIDIA's NVFP4 build with TP8 on one RTX 6000D node. Measured in docker: ready in ~10 min on a cold cache, KV 5,222,157 tokens, answers correct; thinking on by default. FlashInfer autotune is off: with it on, vLLM v0.30.0 hangs on these cards at the whole-model autotune pass. /root/.cache is a hostPath so compiled kernels survive a restart.

NVIDIA's NVFP4 build, prefill/decode disaggregated: TP8 per instance on RTX 6000D nodes, NIXL transfer backend, 2 prefill + 1 decode, with L2 KV-offload to mooncakeStore (global segment 100GB, local buffer 4GB). Production-shape values pinned to the harbor v0.30.0-pd-fix2 image, 0.85 GPU memory utilization and 850Gi shm for the large KV offload; node affinity pins pods to RTX-6000D. ModelRoute deepseek-v4-flash publishes the service via the llm-route openresty gateway.

models.name: glm5.3
models.description: GLM-5.3 quantised to NVFP4, served as "glm-5.3" with SGLang on four or eight B300 GPUs, or vLLM with TP8 and PP2 across two RTX 6000D nodes. The tuned four-GPU B300 variant uses EAGLE speculative decoding and a 150 GiB hierarchical KV cache. Tuning results compare throughput normalized to eight GPUs. The FP4 kernels require Blackwell GPUs.

variants.description: Tuned by LLM AutoTune: TP4 on four B300 GPUs, single node, modelopt_fp4 weights, EAGLE speculative decoding, hierarchical KV cache. Normalized throughput (8 GPUs) within the SLO vs the baseline variant: +195.3% (50k + 1.5k), +30.6% (8k + 1k).
Baseline: TP8 on eight B300 GPUs, single node, modelopt_fp4 weights.

TP8 per node with expert parallel, PP2 across two nodes over RoCE. EP is required, not a tuning choice: plain TP8 cannot load this NVFP4 build. KV pool 1,180,288 tokens, max_req_input_len 1,048,570, and a real 1M-token request completes in 428 s. At 50k/1.5k and concurrency 10: 4,341 input and 126 output tok/s; at 80k/600: 6,722 and 47.6, ahead of the vLLM variant while running 10 concurrent requests against its 17. TTFT is 1.7-3x worse throughout, because prefill queues in 8,192-token chunks.

Prefill/decode-disaggregated DisaggregatedSet, TP8 PP2 EP8 per role on RTX 6000D over RoCE. EP is required, not a tuning choice: plain TP8 cannot load this NVFP4 build. Default 2 prefill + 1 decode; prefill.replicas is configurable at deploy time (xPyD).

Prefill/decode-disaggregated DisaggregatedSet, TP8 PP2 EP8 per role on RTX 6000D over RoCE, with local KV offload via hicache (size 100). EP is required, not a tuning choice: plain TP8 cannot load this NVFP4 build. Default 2 prefill + 1 decode; prefill.replicas is configurable at deploy time (xPyD).
TP8 per node, PP2 across two nodes over RoCE, on the same NVFP4 weights as the B300 variant.
Prefill/decode-disaggregated DisaggregatedSet, TP8 PP2 per role on RTX 6000D, mooncake transfer backend. Default 2 prefill + 1 decode; prefill.replicas is configurable at deploy time (xPyD).

Prefill/decode-disaggregated DisaggregatedSet, TP8 PP2 per role on RTX 6000D, mooncake transfer backend + local KV offload via mooncakeStore (8 GPUs x 100 GB global segment + 8 x 4 GB local buffer per engine). Default 2 prefill + 1 decode; prefill.replicas is configurable at deploy time (xPyD).

TP8 per node, PP4 across four nodes over RoCE. Marlin is the only correct MoE runner here: the default upcasts the MXFP4 experts to bf16 and needs ~6000 GiB, triton_kernel fails in the weight loader, and flashinfer_mxfp4 loads, serves and computes wrong answers. Measured 47.81 GiB of weights per card and max_total_num_tokens 1,237,195.

TP8 per node, PP4 across four nodes over RoCE. A Marlin MoE path is required on sm120, to keep the 4-bit weights 4-bit; the default runner upcasts them to bf16 and does not fit. sglang reaches the same shape with --moe-runner-backend marlin.
